problems.form_value: Population-normalized agent attribution of the stable vocabulary, not a creativity or diversity rating. Words must appear in every one of the final 5 rounds; early human/agent usage is normalized by population share, and attribution scores are weighted by final-round word frequency. Default early-diffusion window is 3 rounds; windows of 1-3 rounds are robustness variants of this same outcome (p. 7, M2; p. 17, equations S1-S3; p. 25, Supplementary Figures 4-5). Higher values mean more AI lexical influence, with no automatic interpretation as greater creativity. This is a descriptive contribution score on the mixed human-agent output pool. The source does not designate primary or secondary outcomes.
problems.source_says: The lexical contribution weights are total word usage counts over the final five rounds, not word frequency in the final round alone. The form correctly states the five-round vocabulary inclusion rule but then changes the weighting window to final-round word frequency. Replace that weighting description with total usage in the final five rounds; the reported contribution values themselves match the figure.
problems.quote: where the weight for each word is its total usage count in the final 5 rounds.
problems.locator: PDF p. 7, Methods M2, Lexical-level contribution, last sentence; p. 17, equation S3 and its following definition.

problems.source_says: Methods M4 defines an objective change in cosine similarity between a player's written expression and the partner's expression; Figure 3b reports early- versus late-game adoption. This output-convergence analysis is absent from studies[].outcomes and is distinct from S1-O2's first-to-final movement toward an initial group centroid. The paper reports human versus agent adoption declines of -0.055 versus -0.020 (U = 671, p < 0.001), and an early-phase human-versus-agent comparison (U = 1735, p < 0.001). These are within-game comparisons of player types, not randomized human AI-versus-control effects. AI co-players remain present; the measure must not be confused with the separate self-reported adoption-willingness questionnaire. The statistical aggregation unit is not explicitly identified.
problems.quote: Adoption quantifies how much a participant moves toward their partner’s expression following an interaction.
problems.locator: PDF p. 9, Methods M4, Measuring adoption, equation 5; p. 4, second paragraph under Initial alignment and adoption–persistence dynamics; p. 14, Figure 3b.

problems.source_says: Persistence is computed from cosine similarity between the same player's consecutive written descriptions, and Figure 3c compares early and late phases with AI still present. The paper reports persistence increases of +0.143 for humans versus +0.059 for agents (U = 1702, p < 0.001), but the outcome has no record. This is objective within-person stability/variation, not diversity across different people and not an after-AI outcome. Human-versus-agent comparisons must remain identified as player-type comparisons; the statistical aggregation unit is not explicitly identified.
problems.quote: Persistence quantifies how stable a participant’s expression is across consecutive rounds.
problems.locator: PDF p. 9, Methods M4, Measuring persistence, equation 6; p. 4, adoption/persistence results; p. 14, Figure 3c.

problems.source_says: The supplement computes directional influence from changes in produced-description embeddings and then assigns each human or agent player a reverse-PageRank score. It reports human-versus-agent score distributions for each agent proportion, with all Mann–Whitney tests p > 0.1. This participant-level, objectively computed influence outcome is mentioned only as an omission in the form's notes, despite the form retaining other output-derived attribution measures. It is an other/with_ai mechanism outcome, not a creativity rating, a diversity score, or a randomized human treatment contrast; exact U statistics and numerical group means are not printed.
problems.quote: To quantify each participant’s overall influence, we compute PageRank on the reversed graph G⊤.
problems.locator: PDF pp. 20–21, Supplementary Information, Influence Network Analysis, equations S6–S7 and final paragraph; p. 28, Supplementary Figure 8b–c.

problems.field: outcomes: missing lexical and conceptual contribution components
problems.source_says: Study C retains the conceptual-lexical ratio but omits its separately reported lexical and conceptual contribution outcomes, although both components are retained for Studies A and B. Supplementary Figure 6 prints default three-round-window lexical contribution of 0.51 for 7B versus 0.61 for 32B, and conceptual contribution of 0.23 versus 0.36. These are rounded printed labels, not values calculated from CLR. Both are objective set-level attribution outcomes produced during AI-present play (other/with_ai); no uncertainty estimates are supplied. A sentence acknowledging the omitted components in S3-O2 does not record their distinct results.
